content.title: About
content.content: Goldfish crackers are small fish‑shaped snacks coated with a savory cheese glaze. Made from wheat flour, vegetable oils and cheese, they have a crunchy texture and a light, slightly salty cheese flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Goldfish were first introduced in the United States in 1962 by Pepperidge Farm.
The fish shape was chosen to make the product instantly recognizable and appealing to children.
More than 20 Goldfish flavors exist, including original cheese, pizza, barbecue and sweet varieties.
In the 2020s the company launched gluten‑free and dairy‑free versions for people with dietary restrictions.
A typical bag contains about 30‑40 pieces, making it a convenient on‑the‑go snack.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Goldfish provide a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains vitamin B2
items.content: The cheese coating supplies a modest amount of riboflavin, which supports energy metabolism.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Wheat flour contributes iron, an essential mineral for blood formation.

items.title: Convenient snack
items.content: Their crunchy texture and bite‑size shape make them a handy snack between meals.

items.title: Gluten and dairy allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat and cheese, which can trigger reactions in allergic individuals.

items.title: High sodium level
items.content: Cheese‑flavored crackers are often salty; excessive sodium intake may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although portions are small, Goldfish are relatively calorie‑dense, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Choking hazard for children
items.content: The small fish shapes can pose a choking risk for young children and should be given under supervision.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Goldfish are perfect straight from the bag, can be added to salads, soups, or used as a garnish. They pair well with dips, yogurt or cheese spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer shelf life keep them in an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption and loss of crunch.
